answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every agent to lock a small non-transferable stake in a shared registry before it may trade. Picture the registry as a shale bed: identities settle into distinct layers, and a random cipher challenge forces each layer to prove it controls a unique ferrous hardware key, a tamper-resistant chip bound to one device. Agents that fail lose their stake and their layer collapses, so spinning up thousands of fake identities costs real hardware and real money, while honest agents keep trading on one verified key.
